issue.close_reason:
ACTIONABLE REJECTION. No repository files were changed and no commit was manufactured. Reviewed committed HEAD 5a8b0c97c160be8f5b876617952be023c6e9be97 without consulting another implementation. ADR-023 has Decision items rather than numbered §§3.2/4.1/4.4; its Decision items 2-5, ADR-024 Decision items 1-5, and normative secret-ruleset-v4 §§3.2, 4.1, 4.4, with §§3.3, 3.4, and 4.5, were the governing references.

Findings: §3.2 clearly defines raw and normalized membership, explicit normalized escape/percent transforms, dewrapped source, decoded source from normalized input, one-level intent from ADR-024 Decision 4/Rationale, and limits of 64 runs per field/65,536 bytes per run. It does not define line-terminator variants, the exact union alphabet, first-64 left-to-right selection, independent-run/slot semantics, over-limit skip versus truncate behavior, invalid-decoding handling, or complete lenient-base64 grammar. §3.4 says smallest raw range and whole-run decoded range but does not make half-open envelope/mapping invariants precise. These gaps can cause missed later/over-limit credentials and divergent fingerprints/redaction selectors.

§4.1/§4.5 make direct JWT blocking normative for three >=8-byte [A-Za-z0-9_-] segments with first two beginning eyJ, only when the first segment decodes to a JSON object containing alg. A fresh synthetic JWT had segments 36/26/16, shape=true, header_alg=true, intended block; the same-shape no-alg case was intended checksum_failed/advisory. A one-level base64url(JWT) probe had a 107-byte encoded run and 80 printable decoded bytes, but decoded-run selection/grammar gaps prevent cross-implementation determinism. §3.3 correctly limits decoded matching to provider/private-key rules.

§4.4 has an unambiguous positive for `-token  <40-byte alternating value>`: Q(value,20) was true (len=40, alnum=40, digits=20, word_run_bytes=0, transitions=39), so that exact marked row is intended to block. The literal form requires a marker; unmarked `token  <value>` is not a Form 3 row. `|token|<value>|` is ambiguous because `|` is allowed by Value but also an optional delimiter, and `| token | <value> |` is not guaranteed because post-marker whitespace is unspecified. Table-row blocking is therefore only partially normative.

Supplied research/fixtures/secret-write-boundary-v1.json is not a v4 truth fixture: jq identity/schema validation passed, all 9 cases were present with expected outcomes direct-service-create reject-before-commit, direct-service-comment reject-before-commit, manifest-late-operation all-or-none-reject, recovered-template-materialize reject-generated-text, managed-mode-downgrade fail-closed, managed-acknowledgment fail-closed, recovery-local-finding local-success-publication-quarantined, quarantined-flush refuse, and redacted-recovery publish-sanitized-generation; the decoded/JWT/table-row marker scan found none. It cannot discharge this review.

Keep BR-T39 through BR-T44 blocked. Revise §3.2 selection/overflow/slot accounting, independent-run boundaries, exact lenient-base64 grammar and decoded source; formalize §3.4 raw half-open mapping; resolve §4.4 marker/whitespace/pipe delimiter precedence and reported spans; add v4 decoded/JWT/table-row truth rows; then perform a new exact-hash review. The clean archive of committed HEAD passed `scripts/definition-of-done.sh --fast` (fmt and full test suite: 332 library tests, 327 binary tests, all integration suites, 2 doctests), the clean-extraction fixture checks, and clean-extraction Clippy. `bead sync flush-only` passed at covered sequence 16808. `git push` reported Everything up-to-date and `git rev-list origin/main..HEAD` was empty. The pre-close status showed only pre-existing shared-worker edits/checkpoint churn plus the bead checkpoint publication; no task-owned source/config/test/docs change was staged.

issue.description: After the qualifier review, inspect ADR-023 sections 3.2, 4.1, and 4.4 plus the corresponding ruleset-v4 sections. Check raw, normalized, dewrapped, and decoded-view boundaries; one-level decoding, bounds, over-limit behavior, decoded-run selection, and lenient base64 grammar; and whether JSON web tokens and table rows are normatively blocked. Exercise the supplied synthetic fixtures without consulting another implementation. Acceptance: record in this bead's notes a pass or actionable rejection with exact section references, fixture outcomes, and any compatibility or detection-gap consequence.
issue.notes:
Disposition: ACTIONABLE REJECTION for the scoped decoded-view/JWT/table-row review; do not accept the current ruleset-v4 hash. Reviewed current bytes: research/specs/secret-ruleset-v4.md SHA-256 bad7c8102086d8128465e284b839673ceceb84b28e3ea7bf55835dfaee5ad5a9; docs/adr/023-widen-blocking-ruleset-to-observed-credential-formats.md SHA-256 39d9174173df3aadc7c268bdd27d139e1091cc12559e20b9d098037683a7359a; docs/adr/024-match-on-a-normalized-view.md SHA-256 508989f43c984b3a69ef529eaaf0d96ed1caa44873857e91b14aeaaa61de9c86; supplied research/fixtures/secret-write-boundary-v1.json SHA-256 c75f4dbf6242ced3c7e21e501e1de7a0fbef2a5371c601957c809043f0996710.

Scope and positive intent: ADR-023 Decision items 2-5 and ADR-024 Decision items 1-5 establish the intended provider/context/structural/labelled coverage and raw-plus-derived matching model. Ruleset-v4 §3.1 says preceding ASCII alphanumeric and following rule-body alphabet bytes reject a provider/context match; §3.2 defines raw, normalized, dewrapped, and decoded views; §3.3 sends blocking rules to raw/normalized/dewrapped and only provider/private-key rules to decoded; §4.1 lists json-web-token as a provider rule; §4.4 says form-3 table rows block at Q(value,20); §4.5 requires JWT header JSON object alg validation before blocking.

Boundary review: raw and normalized view membership is stated, and §3.2 explicitly makes decoded input the normalized view (not dewrapped); ADR-024 Rationale/Decision limits decoding to one level. However, §3.2 does not define line-terminator variants for dewrapping, the exact union alphabet meant by “base64 or base64url alphabet bytes,” or a formal half-open raw-range envelope for a derived match. §3.4 only says “smallest raw range”; it does not state first/last mapped-span envelope, empty-match prohibition, or boundary invariants. This leaves redaction/fingerprint coordinates implementation-dependent.

Decoded bounds/selection: §3.2 gives 40-byte minimum, at-most-64 runs per field, and at-most-65,536 bytes per run, but does not say whether run selection is left-to-right/first-64, whether an over-limit run is skipped or truncated, whether it consumes a run slot, or that each decoded run is an independent view. Synthetic probes: 65 separated 40-byte runs and a 65,537-byte maximal alphabet run have no unique normative outcome. This creates a detection gap for credentials in runs after the unspecified cutoff and a compatibility gap between skip/truncate/slot-count implementations.

Lenient base64: §3.2 names “lenient base64” without specifying padding, unpadded input, padding placement/count, non-zero pad bits, mixed standard and URL alphabets, invalid length modulo 4, or invalid trailing material. In-memory probes showed the choices are observable: canonical Zg== and non-canonical Zh== both decode under a permissive decoder; Zg is an unpadded spelling; A, Z===, Z=g=, and mixed ++++/----____ require policy decisions. A valid one-level base64(JWT) synthetic run was 132 bytes and decoded to printable text, consistent with ADR-024’s one-level intent, but the contract cannot require the same result across implementations.

JWT outcome: an in-memory synthetic JWT with three >=8-character [A-Za-z0-9_-] segments, first two beginning eyJ, and a decoded header object containing alg satisfies §4.1 plus §4.5 and is intended to block. An otherwise shaped synthetic JWT whose decoded header lacks alg fails the §4.5 validation and is intended to be checksum_failed/advisory, not blocking. Direct JWT intent is therefore normatively present, but JWTs found only through decoded-view processing are not deterministically covered until §3.2 selects runs and defines the decoder grammar; a valid JWT in a skipped/over-limit/non-canonical run can be missed or diverge.

Table-row outcome: an in-memory alternating 40-byte alphanumeric value satisfies the literal §2.2 inequalities for Q(value,20) (P=false, a=40, d=20, w=0, t=39). The forms `token  <value>` and `-token  <value>` therefore have a deterministic intended blocking outcome under §4.4. `|token|<value>|` is not deterministic: §4.4 Value excludes whitespace/quotes/backtick/comma/semicolon but does not exclude `|`, while the same form names an optional trailing `|`; the final pipe can be value content or delimiter. `| token | <value> |` is not guaranteed to match because no whitespace after the marker is specified. Thus table-row blocking is intended but not fully normative for the stated pipe/table cases.

Fixture outcomes: research/fixtures/secret-write-boundary-v1.json parsed successfully with all 9 manifest cases present and expected values populated, but it is a write-boundary fixture and contains no v4 view, decoded-run, JWT, or table-row truth rows. No supplied fixture can discharge this review; the in-memory probes above are synthetic review probes only. No other implementation was consulted.

Compatibility/detection consequence: keep BR-T39 through BR-T44 blocked. The intended direct JWT and unambiguous table-row positives preserve the proposed ruleset direction, but accepting this hash would permit divergent findings, fingerprints, and bead-redact selectors, plus misses for later/over-limit/grammar-sensitive decoded credentials and pipe-form rows. Required revision: specify §3.2 first-64 left-to-right selection, over-limit skip/truncate and slot accounting, independent-run boundaries, exact base64 grammar, and dewrapped/decoded source; specify §3.4 raw half-open envelope invariants; and revise §4.4 delimiter precedence, post-marker whitespace, value alphabet, and exact reported span. Add v4 synthetic truth rows for all these cases and issue a new exact-hash review.
Fresh revalidation in the current checkout (HEAD f7c7af1f0e7b31b93e3a3c23760386b333c9acf9): sha256sum reproduced the four reviewed artifacts as secret-ruleset-v4 bad7c8102086d8128465e284b839673ceceb84b28e3ea7bf55835dfaee5ad5a9, ADR-023 39d9174173df3aadc7c268bdd27d139e1091cc12559e20b9d098037683a7359a, ADR-024 508989f43c984b3a69ef529eaaf0d96ed1caa44873857e91b14aeaaa61de9c86, and secret-write-boundary-v1.json c75f4dbf6242ced3c7e21e501e1de7a0fbef2a5371c601957c809043f0996710. jq validation exited 0: contract identity matched, all 9 cases were present, and every case had id/surface/expected fields; the nine outcomes were direct-service-create reject-before-commit, direct-service-comment reject-before-commit, manifest-late-operation all-or-none-reject, recovered-template-materialize reject-generated-text, managed-mode-downgrade fail-closed, managed-acknowledgment fail-closed, recovery-local-finding local-success-publication-quarantined, quarantined-flush refuse, and redacted-recovery publish-sanitized-generation. A marker scan found no decoded/JWT/table-row v4 truth rows, confirming that fixture cannot discharge this review.

Independent in-memory probes reproduced the scoped decisions without consulting another implementation: the alternating 40-byte Q(value,20) candidate had digits=20, alnum=40, word_run_bytes=0, transitions=39, and Q=true; a direct three-segment JWT had shape=true and header_alg=true, while the same-shape no-alg header was intended_block=false/checksum_failed_or_advisory; one-level base64url(JWT) produced a 99-byte run whose decoded bytes were all printable; 65 separated 40-byte runs and a 65,537-byte run exceeded the stated selection/size boundaries; permissive decoding accepted canonical Zg==, non-canonical Zh==, and unpadded Zg; and token/two-space and -token/two-space table rows were unambiguous while pipe delimiter precedence remained unspecified.

The actionable rejection and compatibility/detection consequence are unchanged: the current hash must not be accepted; BR-T39 through BR-T44 remain blocked pending normative §3.2 selection/over-limit/slot/grammar rules, §3.4 mapping invariants, §4.4 table-row delimiter/value-span rules, and v4 decoded/JWT/table-row truth fixtures.
Verification evidence for this retry: the mandatory pre-staging `git status --short` showed only pre-existing shared-worker source/test/config changes plus checkpoint churn; no source, test, documentation, or configuration path was modified by this review, so no repository commit was manufactured. A clean archive of committed HEAD f7c7af1f0e7b31b93e3a3c23760386b333c9acf9 was extracted to /var/tmp/beadrs-ba83ea53-dod-CwEN8g, `scripts/definition-of-done.sh --fast` passed (cargo fmt --check exit 0 and cargo test exit 0; 327 unit tests, all integration suites, and 2 doctests passed), the nine-case jq fixture validation exited 0, the v4-marker absence check exited 0, and the extraction was removed. During that long gate another worker advanced shared HEAD to 5a8b0c9 (`wip(beadrs-9ab1eaaa): assert quarantine remedy guidance`); `git rev-list origin/main..HEAD` currently reports that one unrelated commit, so it was not pushed by this review and the bead was not closed against a non-current upstream.\nCheckpoint durability: /home/coding/.cargo/bin/bead sync flush-only exited 0 and reported the checkpoint already current (covered sequence 16772).
Fresh independent re-review at committed HEAD 5a8b0c97c160be8f5b876617952be023c6e9be97 (no source/test/docs/config paths changed by this review). The requested numbered headings are in the normative ruleset, not ADR-023 itself: ADR-023 has Decision items 2-5; ADR-024 has Decision items 1-5; the exact normative headings are secret-ruleset-v4 §§3.2, 4.1, 4.4, with §3.3, §3.4, and §4.5 controlling view routing, raw reporting, and JWT validation.

Fresh synthetic probe outcomes: Q(value,20) for alternating 40-byte a7... was len=40, alnum=40, digits=20, word_run_bytes=0, transitions=39, true. Direct JWT segments were 36/26/16 bytes, shape=true, both first segments began eyJ, and decoded header JSON had alg, so §4.1 plus §4.5 intends blocking. Same-shape no-alg header had shape=true but header_alg=false, so §4.5 intends checksum_failed/advisory. One-level base64url(JWT) produced a 107-byte encoded run and 80 printable decoded bytes, consistent with ADR-024 Decision 4 and Rationale (one level). Sixty-five separated 40-byte runs exceed §3.2's at-most-64 limit, but first-64/last-64/other selection is unspecified; a 65,537-byte maximal run exceeds the 65,536-byte bound, but skip/truncate/slot behavior is unspecified. The lenient grammar probes remain policy-sensitive: Zg==, Zh==, unpadded Zg, A, Z=g=, and mixed +/-- have no complete normative acceptance/rejection rules.

Table-row correction: §4.4 Form 3 says one list/table marker is present. Therefore `-token  <40-byte alternating value>` is an unambiguous marker-plus-separator Q20 blocking candidate; unmarked `token  <value>` is missing the stated marker and is not normatively a Form 3 match. `|token|<value>|` remains ambiguous because `|` is not excluded from **Value** yet is also an optional delimiter; `| token | <value> |` is not guaranteed because whitespace after the marker is not specified. This tightens, rather than reverses, the actionable rejection.

Supplied fixture recheck: research/fixtures/secret-write-boundary-v1.json parsed successfully; jq schema/identity check exit 0; all 9 cases were present with id/surface/expected fields and outcomes direct-service-create reject-before-commit, direct-service-comment reject-before-commit, manifest-late-operation all-or-none-reject, recovered-template-materialize reject-generated-text, managed-mode-downgrade fail-closed, managed-acknowledgment fail-closed, recovery-local-finding local-success-publication-quarantined, quarantined-flush refuse, and redacted-recovery publish-sanitized-generation. The v4 marker scan exit 0: this supplied fixture has no decoded-view, JWT, or table-row truth rows, so it cannot discharge this review.

Decision remains ACTIONABLE REJECTION for the reviewed hashes (secret-ruleset-v4 bad7c8102086d8128465e284b839673ceceb84b28e3ea7bf55835dfaee5ad5a; ADR-023 39d9174173df3aadc7c268bdd27d139e1091cc12559e20b9d098037683a7359a; ADR-024 508989f43c984b3a69ef529eaaf0d96ed1caa44873857e91b14aeaaa61de9c86; fixture c75f4dbf6242ced3c7e21e501e1de7a0fbef2a5371c601957c809043f0996710). Keep BR-T39 through BR-T44 blocked. Required revision remains: make §3.2 selection, overflow and slot accounting, independent-run boundaries, exact lenient base64 grammar, and decoded source normative; make §3.4 raw half-open mapping invariants normative; resolve §4.4 marker/whitespace/pipe delimiter precedence and reported span; and add v4 truth rows. issue.description:
Auto-split child of beadrs-5a0dc962 (binary-build procedure). Precondition for the parent acceptance criterion that a pinned build reproduces its recorded sha256: build.rs currently embeds wall-clock UTC time via date -u (build.rs lines 42-48) and, in a git-archive tree with no .git, falls back to commit "unknown", so two builds of the same commit can never be byte-identical today.

Scope:
- build.rs: when SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH is set, use it for the embedded build timestamp instead of invoking date; otherwise keep current behavior.
- build.rs: allow the short commit sha to be supplied by the environment (e.g. BEAD_COMMIT_SHA) for archive builds that have no .git; keep "unknown" as the fallback.
- Keep the NEEDLE-visible version-string shape unchanged: leading bare program name plus a parenthesised detail block.
- Test asserting: same tree + same SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH + same commit override = identical binary sha256 across two different CARGO_TARGET_DIRs; differing SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH = differing sha256.

Acceptance:
- Two fresh builds of the same commit with identical SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH and commit override, in two different target dirs, produce identical sha256.
- Default behavior without SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH is unchanged (wall-clock timestamp, "unknown" commit in archive trees).
- Existing --version output format still parses the way NEEDLE expects.

Parent: beadrs-5a0dc962.
issue.title: Make build.rs builds reproducible via SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH and a commit-sha override
